clue.text: Before test, have cigarette as a distraction

parts.note: to have a cigarette is to smoke
to screen is to test, as in medical screening

explanation.surface: Someone nervously lights up before an exam to take their mind off it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before test' tells you the cigarette word comes first, ahead of the test word.
explanation.definitionFit: A smokescreen is anything used to hide intentions or divert attention, so it serves as a distraction.

clue.text: Material source of comfort

parts.note: surface reading: some physical thing, such as money or possessions, that makes life comfortable
setter's reading: literally a piece of fabric that comforts, like the one a small child clings to

explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like it means worldly goods; it is literal cloth, the blanket a child carries for reassurance.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a child's comfort blanket and, by extension, anything familiar a person relies on for reassurance.

clue.text: Creature receives oxygen and potassium quietly in first class

indicators.note: one thing placed in another is enclosed by it, so the quiet sign sits inside the class

parts.note: chemical symbol for oxygen
chemical symbol for potassium
A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as the letter I
p, piano, is the musical mark for playing quietly

explanation.surface: An animal is given gas and a mineral supplement in a quiet, upmarket setting.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (written AI) is the old shipping-register mark for top quality.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is an African animal related to the giraffe, so it is an example of a creature.

clue.text: Given to alter appearance without notice when copping out

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the rearranged letters wrap round the notice
changing how something looks means its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: Someone disguises themselves without warning while dodging a responsibility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside: the rearranged letters split around the notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Copping out means dodging a duty, and evading is the same kind of avoidance.

clue.text: Complain about opposing European union redistribution

indicators.note: about means around, so the complaint word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to carp is to complain
v for versus, meaning against
standard abbreviation for European
standard abbreviation for union

explanation.surface: A grumble about anti-EU politics and the reallocation of resources.
explanation.definitionFit: A carve-up is a sharing out of something among parties, often unfairly, which is a redistribution.

clue.text: Not hard, one hears, to come upon soft target

parts.note: easy is the opposite of hard

indicators.note: what one hears is a sound, so the word for come upon is chosen by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: to meet is to come upon; it sounds like the food word

explanation.surface: An easily found, vulnerable target is described as simple to stumble upon.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy meat is an idiom for a person or thing easily beaten or exploited, a soft target.

clue.text: Doesn't seem attractive to thank locum too carelessly

definitions.note: a verb phrase defining an adjectival phrase: it 'is not much to look at'

indicators.note: something done carelessly ends up out of order, so these words are jumbled

parts.note: all fifteen letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient's careless thank-you note to a stand-in doctor is unflattering.
explanation.walkthrough: A locum is a doctor standing in for another.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying someone is not much to look at is the idiom for plain or unattractive in appearance.

clue.text: Pompous lot are very fed up when Trish mistakenly gets Sun?

parts.note: stuffed means full to bursting, overfed

indicators.note: a name written mistakenly comes out in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
S is the abbreviation for Sunday

explanation.surface: Stuck-up people are annoyed when Trish wrongly receives a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' looks like annoyed, but 'very fed' means overfull. The Sun is a British tabloid, which helps the surface; here it is just Sunday's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffed shirt is a pompous, self-important person, so the plural is a pompous lot.

clue.text: Hard material from the opera confused student

indicators.note: confused letters are mixed up and have to be put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A tough piece of music from an opera bewilders a music student.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother-of-pearl is nacre, the hard iridescent substance lining some shells.

clue.text: Repeatedly act out absorbing love for music

indicators.note: something absorbing another takes it inside itself
out can mean disordered, so the doubled word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word act given twice
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A performer keeps acting out a passion for music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeatedly' doubles the word before it is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a fast keyboard piece showing off the player's touch, an example of music.

clue.text: Return to teacher to get food

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the following words are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
pupils address a male teacher as sir
the second to, taken as written

explanation.surface: A pupil goes back to the teacher in order to be fed.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish, an example of food.

clue.text: Promote growth, if sterile otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters are arranged differently

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to boost growth if the soil is barren.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is neat because fertile is the opposite of sterile.
explanation.definitionFit: To fertilise is to add nutrients or pollen, encouraging plants or eggs to develop and grow.

clue.text: Speak silently at opening

definitions.meaning: first meaning: form words with the lips without sound
second meaning: an entrance, as of a cave or river

explanation.surface: Someone mimes their words at the start of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means forming words soundlessly; as a noun it is an opening such as a cave entrance.

clue.text: Takes in second game during mixed set

indicators.note: during means within, so one piece sits inside the other
mixed letters are jumbled into another order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: second points to the letter in position two of the next word

parts.note: the second letter of game

explanation.surface: A tennis commentary: a second game played within a muddled set.
explanation.walkthrough: The tennis words game and set are pure decoys.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat is to take food in, so eats matches takes in in the third person.

clue.text: Kitchen equipment gets one into hot water

definitions.text: Kitchen equipment gets one into hot water

parts.note: surface reading: lands someone in trouble, as if the kitchen gadget caused a row
setter's reading: literally placing an item of food into simmering water to cook it

explanation.walkthrough: 'One' looks like a person in trouble; it is the food item being lowered into the pan.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg poacher is a pan with cups that cooks eggs over simmering water.

clue.text: Flower sprang up from underground

parts.note: the Tube is the London Underground
rose is the past tense of rise, to spring up

explanation.surface: A bloom pushes up out of the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' lets the underground word come first, and 'underground' is not soil but London's Tube railway.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuberose is a fragrant white-flowered plant, an example of a flower.

clue.text: Unconventional group advance the arts

parts.note: a sub is an advance of money against wages
culture is the arts collectively

explanation.surface: An avant-garde collective pushes the arts forward.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage to sub someone is to lend them money in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: A subculture is a group within society whose values differ from the mainstream, an unconventional group.

clue.text: Merry men, without a leader, screw up

indicators.note: having no leader means the front letter is dropped

parts.note: merry and tight are both informal for slightly drunk
taken as written, before its first letter goes

explanation.surface: Robin Hood's Merry Men, leaderless, make a mess of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merry men' suggests Robin Hood's band, but merry means tipsy and the men lose their head.
explanation.definitionFit: To screw up a bolt or lid is to turn it tighter, so to tighten it.

clue.text: New edition refers to children

parts.note: re means regarding, used to say what something refers to
issue is the formal word for offspring

explanation.surface: A revised book now includes mention of children.
explanation.definitionFit: A reissue is a book or record published again, a new edition of an existing work.

clue.text: Run back to find animal

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to flow is to run, as liquid does

explanation.surface: An instruction to retrace one's steps to spot an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The wolf is a wild dog, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Double vision

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a picture in the mind

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words are the eye condition; they are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person's exact likeness and a mental picture or visualisation.

clue.text: Aim to accept it, only to leave partner

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so the aim word holds the pronoun inside

parts.note: a goal is an aim
taken as written
one can mean only, as in my one chance

explanation.surface: Someone plans to put up with things, only to walk out on their partner anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: To go it alone is the idiom for acting independently, which is what leaving a partner means.

clue.text: Shall we have another oven at home?

definitions.note: the answer, spoken as a question, means the same as this whole phrase

parts.note: an Aga is a British make of range cooker
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A host asks whether to buy a second range cooker for the house.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a heavy cast-iron range cooker, a fixture of British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'Again?' asks for a repeat, the same request as asking whether to have another.

clue.text: Destroy produce from within

definitions.meaning: first meaning: kill or eliminate a target
second meaning: bring something out of a pocket or bag

explanation.surface: A demolition and an extraction seem to describe a factory's fate.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to eliminate an enemy and to remove an object from a container.

clue.text: One won't try to become more relaxed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person who avoids effort
second meaning: comparative of slack, looser

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to make any effort to loosen up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' sounds like rugby scoring but simply means make an effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A slacker is a lazy person who shirks work, and slacker is also the comparative of slack, meaning looser.

clue.text: Communications system is alien to the trainee

parts.note: taken as written
an intern is a trainee on a work placement
ET, the extra-terrestrial of the film

explanation.surface: A newcomer finds the office network completely foreign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' means added to: the alien comes after the trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: The internet is the global computer network, a system for communications.
